title: Hive Mind Gate Extension Frontmatter
description: Required frontmatter on every gate-extension file under the path declared by `extensions.gates` in hive.yml. A gate extension declares one additional pre-push check that runs AFTER the built-in Sentinel pattern scan has passed. Gates are additive only — they cannot suppress a built-in match, and they cannot disable the Sentinel. `assets/generate-hook.sh` bakes declared gates into the generated pre-push hook at generation time, so the emitted hook keeps zero runtime dependencies of its own.

layer.description: Always `PROTOCOL`. Gate extensions govern what may be pushed, so they are protocol surface — changes go via CODEOWNERS PR, never the inbox or Parliament.

type.description: Discriminator. The hook generator loads only files carrying this type from the declared gates path; anything else in the directory is ignored.

gate.description: Short name for this gate, shown to the contributor in pass/block output (e.g. `llm-compliance-review`). Must match the filename stem.

command.description: Shell command to run, resolved relative to the Hive root. The candidate file list is appended as positional arguments ("$@") — the same list the pattern scan saw. The command receives HIVE_ROOT and APIARY_SENTINEL_PASSED=1 in its environment. Exit 0 allows the push; any non-zero exit blocks it (subject to `on_error`). Keep the command in-repo (e.g. `python3 scripts/compliance_gate.py`) so it is reviewable alongside the gate declaration.

description.description: One line: what this gate checks and why the built-in pattern scan is insufficient for it. This is the justification a reviewer reads — 'catches program-specific content that names no program, which no regex can match' is the shape wanted.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 date of most recent update.

codeowners.description: GitHub usernames who approve changes to this gate. A gate is a security control; changing it should require the same review as changing the Sentinel patterns.

on_error.description: What happens when the gate cannot run or exits non-zero. `block` (default) fails closed: the push is refused. `warn` fails open: the failure is reported and the push proceeds. Default to `block` — a gate that degrades to 'allow' is worse than no gate once contributors trust it. Use `warn` only for advisory checks, and say why in `description`.
on_error.$comment: Any value other than the literal string 'warn' is normalized to 'block' by the generator, so a typo fails closed rather than open.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit for the gate command. 0 means no limit. A timeout is treated as a non-zero exit and therefore honors `on_error`. Requires `timeout(1)`; when absent the gate runs unbounded. Set this on any gate making a network or model call so a hung dependency cannot wedge every contributor's push.

required_tools.description: Executables that must be on PATH for the gate to run, checked before invocation so a missing dependency produces an actionable message instead of an opaque non-zero exit. Missing tools honor `on_error`. Declare everything beyond bash/grep/git — e.g. [python3, claude].

classification.description: Classification of the content in this file. Optional by default; required when the Hive's `hive.yml` sets `classification.marking_required: true`. Must not exceed the Hive's `classification.max_level`.
